key_insight: Experimentally trained surrogate models can forecast cylinder-wake evolution faster than real time, but their accuracy degrades as flow details become more transient, noisy, and high frequency.
engineering_relevance: This work shows how learned flow models could support practical flow control and prediction from imperfect PIV measurements, while highlighting the limits engineers must account for in real-world sensing.
method: Train fully convolutional neural networks, U-Nets, Fourier neural operators, and DMD-based models
Use 2D, 2-component PIV cylinder-wake data for time-evolution forecasting
Evaluate both fixed-Re long-horizon prediction and multi-Re generalization from Re = 230 to 2920
evidence_signal: Models produced meaningful short-horizon forecasts and faster-than-real-time inference, but struggled to preserve transient structures and high-frequency energy under noisy, incomplete observations.
watch_item: Performance may drop sharply when measurements are incomplete or imperfect, especially for more turbulent and three-dimensional flow regimes.
paper_title: Data-driven surrogate models for forecasting experimentally measured fluid flows
